title: Turning the 121-trait catalog into scales: which words are opposite ends, and the rules each scale's tuning follows
question: The game's traits are scales between two opposite ends. The personality catalog researched on 2026-09-21 is a list of 121 single words. Which of those words pair as the two ends of one scale, which stand alone as one end with a plain opposite, and which are aliases of the same scale? For each resulting scale, what rule should decide how strongly people hold it, how it is spread across a starting population, which kinds of decision may read it, whether people are born with it or only acquire it, and how hard it is to change?
whyItMatters: The catalog cannot enter the game until this is answered. Only its names and meanings map onto what the engine stores; every trait the engine loads also needs two opposite ends and a set of tuning values, and the catalog deliberately carries none of them. Filling them by engineering guess would decide how every person in the game behaves without anyone having designed it. Meanwhile the game ships five abstract axes, and lamontae ranks personality first.
usableAnswer: Two things. First, a grouping of the 121 catalog ids into scales: each scale names its two ends (by catalog id where the catalog has the word, otherwise a proposed plain word), and every catalog id appears exactly once, as an end, an alias of an end, or explicitly set aside with a reason. Second, for each tuning dimension, a rule for how it varies between kinds of scale rather than a number per trait — for example, which families of scale should be harder to change than others, which should be something a person is born with versus something they acquire, and which kinds of decision each family is allowed to inform. Rules that vary, not constants; no per-trait numbers are wanted, and none have been approved.

sourcesChecked.source: The personality catalog, /mnt/project-files/research/personality/personality-catalogue.json (schema ocd-personality-research/1, research date 2026-09-21), with its .md and .xlsx renders and validation.json
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: 121 candidates in 14 families, 29 separate concepts, 20 sources. Every candidate carries the same eleven fields: id, name, family, source_ids, source_locator, proposed_meaning, ordinary_life_example, public_role_example, boundary, status, source_urls. All 121 are marked 'RESEARCH CANDIDATE — not implemented; final module selection/behavior requires review'. Its own rules say no trait count, weights, prevalence or change rate is approved, and that aliases may share one mechanism. It does not pair any word with an opposite and carries no tuning of any kind.

sourcesChecked.source: The catalog's claim that its text is original
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Its rules state that every proposal field is original design and that no descriptions are copied from the games and mods it cites (a Sims 4 custom-trait spreadsheet, Sims 4 mods, Crusader Kings III development diaries and others). This thread did NOT verify that claim against any of those sources. It is recorded here as the catalog's own assertion, not as a checked fact.

Establishes what a loaded trait must carry: a key, label and description, two poles each with a key, label and description, a scale of strengths, the decision scopes that may read it, who confers it (seeded, player or conferred-only), a seed spread for seeded traits, and five movability values. It says what the fields are, not what any catalog trait's values should be.

sourcesChecked.source: lamontae's own answers, 2026-09-22 (owner record 01, section A)
sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: People start with one or two traits, and every character can change with varying resistance. That settles how many a person holds and that resistance must vary; it says nothing about which words pair, or how resistance should vary between kinds of trait.

notes: Distinct from person-starting-trait-count (how many traits one person starts with) and from people-and-life's ordinary-life-trait-set (how large the vocabulary should be). This one takes the existing 121 as given and asks how they become scales.

The engine half — a loader, a trait field in content packs, the registry reading installed packs, and the person card reading loaded packs instead of the fixed five — is engineering, not research, and is written up separately in docs/reports/owner-record/08-trait-loader-job.md.
Do not answer with a page of per-trait numbers. lamontae's standing rule is that proposed values are not a thing to put to him, and the catalog itself says none are approved.

answer.summary:
Partly advanced by ChatGPT's proposed 121-candidate classification: only four words pairs are scale ends (deliberate/impulsive, dependable/unreliable, confrontational/conciliatory, cautious/risk-taking); 112 are descriptors and teasing is set aside as a form of playful. Owner answer it records: use descriptors and scales together. See traits-held-at-once for the full summary.

Earlier answer (2026-09-22T18:27:00.000Z), kept:

## A01 — All 121 personality candidates have an explicit disposition

**Question:** `trait-catalog-poles-and-tuning-rules`.

The 121-word catalog did not itself answer how a two-ended loader should encode it. The supplied mapping answers every original ID without silently treating all neighboring adjectives as opposites.

Eighteen selected bipolar distinctions are useful as opposing *defaults in a specified context*: insecure/self-assured, solitude-seeking/gregarious, serious/playful, deliberate/impulsive, effort-averse/industrious, unreliable/dependable, irresponsible/responsible, callous/compassionate, suspicious/trusting, disloyal/loyal, deceitful/honest, stubborn/flexible, conciliatory/confrontational, impatient/patient, cautious/risk-taking, timid/brave, stoic/emotionally expressive, and pessimistic/optimistic. The JSON preserves exact catalog IDs and meanings. These are authored game distinctions, not a claim that research identifies eighteen universal psychological factors.

**Cocky is not the opposite of humble. Studious is not the opposite of carefree.** Where a word describes a distinct marked facet, the other end is merely “no marked occurrence of this facet,” not an invented virtue, vice or diagnosis. Someone can be confident without being arrogant, ambitious without being competitive, and reserved without being shy.

The 84 one-sided facets preserve that distinction. `eccentric` is retained as a possible observed presentation of unconventional habits but set aside as an independent numerical decision force: its broad meaning cannot by itself specify what someone wants or decides. This is not deletion of unconventional people.

### The actual engine does not require a wholesale rewrite

`trait-packs.ts` currently asks for two poles and an explicit scale, but `mind-catalog.ts` already permits one expression and contains one-expression curiosity, loyalty and ambition definitions. Therefore a narrow one-sided value policy/adapter at the existing trait-pack layer is sufficient where needed; do not build another mind store.

For compatibility a one-sided facet can declare an unmarked end, but a symmetric generator must not draw a negative magnitude and call it the fabricated opposite. Read and generate only the marked/unmarked meanings the facet defines. Preserve a separate **unknown/unobserved** condition. Lack of evidence is not proof that a person is unmarked.

Keep the existing five system-one axes. Where a new label is exactly an existing meaning, alias it to the actual qualified definition and do not apply the same influence twice. One or two prominent adult descriptors are not the entirety of a person, a trait-screen quota or a permanent lifetime cap. The 102 proposed scale/facet definitions are a shared catalog; they are not a demand to allocate or update 102 mandatory fields on every named resident every day.

### Relative tuning, not 121 arbitrary constants

The seven supplied profiles cover appraisal/self-image, manner, cognition, follow-through, motivation, relational orientation and responses under pressure. Each states strength evidence, starting spread, relevant decision scopes, conferral and change rules. These scopes are proposed receiving meanings; they are not claimed as already registered decision IDs.

Strength reflects the breadth and persistence of a freely expressed pattern, with opportunity and constraints retained. Initial “seeded” adult qualities arise from the generated lived person; this does not mean a baby has an adult achievement or a biological destiny. Household wealth, race, gender, degree and job title do not diagnose personality.

Manner and habits can adapt with sustained new circumstances; broad self-image and approach require broader evidence. Actual relationships, goals, knowledge and temporary states often change before a core disposition. The current anti-repetition and finite-resistance work should remain; this answer does not recreate already removed per-change permanent hardening.

**Acceptance:** every catalog ID resolves once; no false opposite; existing base meanings remain; same person across home/work/government; off-context traits do not vote on irrelevant choices; factual knowledge and abilities are not conferred by adjectives; known-unmarked differs from unknown; adding synonyms does not multiply prevalence.
